findings.description: Grader 1.3.0 introduces a head_dir fallback to "$workspace/pr/head" when EVAL_HEAD_DIR is unset and the manifest-side fixture head is absent. The workspace is the agent-writable sandbox (ablation-grade.sh's own header states sandbox pr/ is tamperable and must never be read). The new validity and same-scope rules are computed from head_lines()/scope_map() over that directory, so the graded party controls the inputs that decide credit: padding a file defeats the 'b <= line count' validity rule, deleting the file removes the bound entirely (head_lines returns None, so valid_cite skips the check), and rewriting definition headers can place many defect sites in one <=400-line function so a single citation credits them all via clause (ii). scope_map is also O(lines x headers) for deeply nested headers, so a crafted multi-megabyte head file can stall the grader.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller that invokes the grader with a sandbox workspace and no EVAL_HEAD_DIR grades recall against agent-modified files, inflating defect_catch_rate and credits_function_only; a hostile or over-eager agent can also force a grader timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the "$workspace/pr/head" fallback (or gate it behind an explicit opt-in flag) and require EVAL_HEAD_DIR or the manifest-side fixture head; when neither exists, disable clause (ii) and the bounds check rather than falling back to sandbox content. Cap the number of headers processed in scope_map, or break the span-fill loop with an interval structure, to bound the O(n^2) worst case.

findings.description: The 1.4 row writer reads the sandbox's .loa.config.yaml (agent-writable) to decide dissent_absent_reason. An agent that sets flatline_protocol.enabled: false, or the gate's .enabled: false, has its missing dissent recorded as the planned reason 'disabled' rather than 'error', which the report then treats as an intended arm property. The harness's authoritative copies under eval/ and meta/ are not consulted for this decision. yq also parses attacker-shaped YAML here (anchor/alias expansion), though mikefarah yq bounds this reasonably.
findings.failure_mode: Dissent gates silenced from inside the sandbox are misclassified as deliberately disabled in the ablation report, hiding agent interference with the review/audit gates.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the 'disabled' reason from the arm toggles (meta/arm-evidence.txt dissent=/flatline= lines, written by the harness before the first phase) and from the loa_config_sha256 integrity record, not from the sandbox config; if the sandbox config must be read, compare its sha256 against the recorded value and treat a mismatch as 'error' or 'tampered'.

findings.description: budget_cents_max accepts any whole number up to 15 digits (about $10 trillion in cents). Under budget_scale: diff the effective budget is max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate x 1.2)) capped only by budget_cents_max, so the configured budget_cents no longer bounds spend at all; the estimate can never exceed 1.2 x itself, so the only operative cap is budget_cents_max. In the eval harness the config file lives in the agent-writable sandbox, so an agent can raise that single value and remove the spend ceiling for the gates that run against its own work.
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded API spend on a single gate run when the config is writable by an untrusted party; operators enabling 'diff' may not realise budget_cents stops acting as a cap.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply a sane absolute ceiling to budget_cents_max (for example the same upper bound _conf_uint uses, or a hard 10,000-cent maximum) and fail closed to 'fixed' above it; alternatively keep budget_cents as an absolute floor-and-ceiling pair (never exceed budget_cents_max AND never exceed N x budget_cents). In the harness, have the eval config variant pin budget_cents_max and record its sha256 so sandbox edits are detected.

findings.description: On the schema-enforced branch the numeric-anchor filter is applied via _adv_keep_numeric_anchor, but any jq failure or empty output falls back to the raw finding (candidate="$finding"). The wire schema now requires anchor_line/anchor_line_end and admits null, so a failed filter lets a null or out-of-range line through into the envelope, contradicting the documentation schema (integer, minimum 1) and the stated invariant that an enforced payload 'must not carry one through'. Downstream graders read anchor_line to build path:line pointers.
findings.failure_mode: Consumers of the envelope receive null or absurd anchor_line values on the enforced path under jq error conditions, breaking schema consumers that trust the integer contract.
findings.suggested_fix: On filter failure, strip the two keys explicitly (jq 'del(.anchor_line, .anchor_line_end)') instead of restoring the raw finding, or treat filter failure as a rejection of that finding.
